title: LG Electronics shares to be in focus as promoter to sell 2% stake to meet public float norms; check details | Stock Market News
text:
LG Electronics, a leading single-brand home appliances player, is likely to be on investors' radar in Thursday's trade, as its promoter, LG Electronics Inc., is set to offload a 2% stake in the company through a block deal. The floor price has been set at ₹1,709.30 per share, according to the company's filing. The offer involves the sale of up to 13.58 million shares, worth up to ₹2,320.5 crore. The promoter will be subject to a 180-day lock-in period, during which it will be restricted from selling any further stake in the company. The proposed stake sale is part of the promoter's efforts to meet the minimum public shareholding (MPS) requirements. MPS is a regulatory requirement in India that mandates listed companies to maintain a minimum percentage of their total equity share capital in the hands of non-promoter public shareholders, typically 25%. "The promoter of the company, LG Electronics Inc., has conveyed its intention to sell certain equity shares held by it for compliance with the requirements of minimum public shareholding applicable to the company," the company said in its filing. The shareholding of LG Electronics Inc. as of November 25, 2026, stood at 85% of the company's total issued and paid-up equity share capital. Upon completion of the proposed sale, the promoter's shareholding in the company will decline from 85% to 83%. Earlier this month, the company reported a 25.65% year-on-year rise in its net profit to ₹489.34 crore for the September quarter of FY27. Its revenue from operations increased 19.53% to ₹7,380.04 crore during the quarter, compared with ₹6,174.03 crore in the corresponding period a year ago. Revenue from the Home Appliance & Air Solutions (H&A) segment rose 20.86% to ₹4,771.69 crore in the quarter under review, compared with ₹3,947.85 crore in the year-ago period. The H&A business includes air conditioners, refrigerators, microwave ovens, washing machines, dishwashers, compressors, water purifiers and air purifiers. The segment recorded its "highest growth since listing", driven by strong double-digit growth across key categories. Revenue from the Home Entertainment (HE) segment grew 17.16% year-on-year to ₹2,608.35 crore in Q2 FY27. The segment reported its "third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth" despite a high base, the company added. The HE segment includes televisions (flat-panel TVs, signage, projectors and monitor TVs), audio-visual products, monitors and personal computers. In terms of operating profitability, EBITDA rose 28% to ₹701 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded 63 basis points to 9.5%. Meanwhile, the company also announced its entry into a new B2B segment, Vehicle Solutions, with a focus on in-vehicle infotainment (IVI).
